   775→    def _loss_step(
   776→        self, batch: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]
   777→    ) -> (torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor):
   778→
   779→        # Both are shape [b, s]
   780→        tokens, labels = batch["tokens"], batch["labels"]
   781→
   782→        # Get the attention mask and position ids from the dataset if they
   783→        # exist. Currently, only sample packing in PackedDataset returns these
   784→        mask = batch.get("mask", None)  # shape [b, s, s]
   785→        input_pos = batch.get("input_pos", None)  # shape [b, s]
   786→
   787→        # run model
   788→        logits = self._model(tokens, mask=mask, input_pos=input_pos)
   789→
   790→        # Shift labels to compute loss
   791→        # equivalent to doing labels[..., 1:] and logits[..., :-1, :]
   792→        # But this way we dont need to slice the logits. We just add an ignore index to labels.
   793→        labels = torch.hstack(
   794→            (labels[..., 1:], self.ignore_labels_cache[: labels.shape[0]])
   795→        )
   796→        if not isinstance(logits, list):
   797→            labels = labels.reshape(-1)
   798→            logits = logits.reshape(-1, logits.size(-1))
   799→
   800→        # Compute KD loss
   801→        with torch.no_grad():
   802→            teacher_logits = self._teacher_model(tokens, mask=mask, input_pos=input_pos)
   803→
   804→        # Compute kd loss
   805→        kd_loss = self._kd_loss_fn(logits, teacher_logits, labels)
   806→
   807→        # Compute loss
   808→        loss = self._loss_fn(logits, labels)
   809→
   810→        # free logits otherwise it peaks backward memory
   811→        del logits
   812→        del teacher_logits
   813→
   814→        return loss, kd_loss

   816→    def train(self) -> None:

   818→        The core training loop.
   819→        """

   823→        world_size, rank = training.get_world_size_and_rank()

   825→        # zero out the gradients before starting training
   826→        self._optimizer.zero_grad()
   827→
   828→        # Initialize tokens count and running loss (for grad accumulation)
   829→        t0 = time.perf_counter()
   830→        running_class_loss = 0
   831→        running_kd_loss = 0
   832→        num_tokens = 0

   834→        self._profiler.start()
   835→        # self.epochs_run should be non-zero when we're resuming from a checkpoint

   837→            # Update the sampler to ensure data is correctly shuffled across epochs
   838→            # in case shuffle is True
   839→            self._sampler.set_epoch(curr_epoch)
   840→
   841→            pbar = tqdm(total=self._steps_per_epoch, disable=not (rank == 0))
   842→            for idx, batch in enumerate(self._dataloader):
   843→                if (
   844→                    self.max_steps_per_epoch is not None
   845→                    and (idx // self._gradient_accumulation_steps)
   846→                    == self.max_steps_per_epoch
   847→                ):
   848→                    break
   849→
   850→                # Start tracking CUDA memory for active steps for just the first epoch
   851→                if (
   852→                    self._is_rank_zero
   853→                    and curr_epoch == 0
   854→                    and self.profiler_profile_memory
   855→                    and idx == self.profiler_wait_steps + self.profiler_warmup_steps
   856→                ):
   857→                    torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()

   859→                utils.batch_to_device(batch, self._device)
   860→
   861→                # Calculate the number of unmasked tokens in the current batch
   862→                # and increment the total number of tokens seen in the step
   863→                current_num_tokens = (
   864→                    batch["labels"] != self._loss_fn.ignore_index
   865→                ).sum()
   866→                num_tokens += current_num_tokens

   869→                running_class_loss += class_loss * current_num_tokens
   870→                running_kd_loss += kd_loss * current_num_tokens
   871→                current_loss = (
   872→                    1 - self._kd_ratio
   873→                ) * class_loss + self._kd_ratio * kd_loss

   877→                if (idx + 1) % self._gradient_accumulation_steps == 0:

   881→                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(running_class_loss)
   882→                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(running_kd_loss)

   884→                    training.scale_grads(self._model, 1 / num_tokens)

   886→                    kd_loss_to_log = running_kd_loss.item() / num_tokens

   893→                    class_loss_to_log = class_loss.item()
   894→                    kd_loss_to_log = kd_loss.item()

   896→                        1 - self._kd_ratio
   897→                    ) * class_loss_to_log + self._kd_ratio * kd_loss_to_log
   898→                    pbar.update(1)

   905→                        self.global_step % self._log_every_n_steps == 0

   911→                            "class_loss": class_loss_to_log,
   912→                            "kd_loss": kd_loss_to_log,

   923→                            step=self.global_step,

   928→                    running_kd_loss = 0

    26→"""
    27→Component builders for the Llama2 model and popular variants such as LoRA.
    28→
    29→torchtune provides composable building blocks. Builder functions help
    30→stitch these building blocks into higher-level components. This design has
    31→two benefits:
    32→- The building blocks themselves are very flexible. For example, ``MultiHeadAttention``
    33→can take either nn.Linear or nn.LoRALinear for ``q_proj``.
    34→- Builder functions expose a set of configurable params which keep the constructors of
    35→the building blocks simple.

    39→# ------------------ Vanilla Llama2 ------------------
    40→
    41→
    42→def llama2(
    43→    vocab_size: int,
    44→    num_layers: int,
    45→    num_heads: int,
    46→    num_kv_heads: int,
    47→    embed_dim: int,
    48→    max_seq_len: int,
    49→    attn_dropout: float = 0.0,
    50→    intermediate_dim: Optional[int] = None,
    51→    norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
    52→    rope_base: float = 10000.0,
    53→) -> TransformerDecoder:
    54→    """
    55→    Build the decoder associated with the Llama2 model. This includes:
    56→    - Token embeddings
    57→    - num_layers number of TransformerSelfAttentionLayer blocks
    58→    - RMS Norm layer applied to the output of the transformer
    59→    - Final projection into token space
    60→
    61→    Args:
    62→        vocab_size (int): number of tokens in vocabulary.
    63→        num_layers (int): number of layers in the transformer decoder.
    64→        num_heads (int): number of query heads. For MHA this is also the
    65→            number of heads for key and value
    66→        num_kv_heads (int): number of key and value heads. User should ensure
    67→            `num_heads` % `num_kv_heads` == 0. For standard MHA set `num_kv_heads` == `num_heads`,
    68→            for GQA `num_kv_heads` < `num_heads`, and for MQA set `num_kv_heads` == 1.
    69→        embed_dim (int): embedding dimension for self-attention
    70→        max_seq_len (int): maximum sequence length the model will be run with, as used
    71→            by :func:`~torchtune.modules.KVCache`
    72→        attn_dropout (float): dropout value passed onto scaled_dot_product_attention.
    73→            Default: 0.0
    74→        intermediate_dim (Optional[int]): intermediate dimension for MLP. If not specified,
    75→            this is computed using :func:`~torchtune.modules.scale_hidden_dim_for_mlp`
    76→        norm_eps (float): epsilon in RMS norms.
    77→        rope_base (float): base for rotary embeddings. Default: 10000.0
    78→
    79→    Returns:
    80→        TransformerDecoder: Instantiation of Llama2 model.
    81→    """
    82→    head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
    83→    num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads if num_kv_heads else num_heads
    84→
    85→    rope = RotaryPositionalEmbeddings(
    86→        dim=head_dim, max_seq_len=max_seq_len, base=rope_base
    87→    )
    88→    self_attn = MultiHeadAttention(
    89→        embed_dim=embed_dim,
    90→        num_heads=num_heads,
    91→        num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
    92→        head_dim=head_dim,
    93→        q_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_heads * head_dim, bias=False),
    94→        k_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False),
    95→        v_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False),
    96→        output_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim, bias=False),
    97→        pos_embeddings=rope,
    98→        kv_cache=None,
    99→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   100→        attn_dropout=attn_dropout,
   101→    )
   102→    hidden_dim = (
   103→        intermediate_dim if intermediate_dim else scale_hidden_dim_for_mlp(embed_dim)
   104→    )
   105→    mlp = llama2_mlp(dim=embed_dim, hidden_dim=hidden_dim)
   106→    layer = TransformerSelfAttentionLayer(
   107→        attn=self_attn,
   108→        mlp=mlp,
   109→        sa_norm=RMSNorm(dim=embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   110→        mlp_norm=RMSNorm(dim=embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   111→    )
   112→    tok_embeddings = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
   113→    output_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, vocab_size, bias=False)
   114→    return TransformerDecoder(
   115→        tok_embeddings=tok_embeddings,
   116→        layers=layer,
   117→        num_layers=num_layers,
   118→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   119→        num_heads=num_heads,
   120→        head_dim=head_dim,
   121→        norm=RMSNorm(embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   122→        output=output_proj,
   123→    )

   126→def llama2_mlp(dim: int, hidden_dim: int, quantize_base: bool = False) -> FeedForward:
   127→    """
   128→    Build the MLP layer associated with the Llama model.
   129→    """
   130→    gate_proj = (
   131→        nn.Linear(dim, hidden_dim, bias=False)
   132→        if not quantize_base
   133→        else FrozenNF4Linear(dim, hidden_dim, bias=False)
   134→    )
   135→    down_proj = (
   136→        nn.Linear(hidden_dim, dim, bias=False)
   137→        if not quantize_base
   138→        else FrozenNF4Linear(hidden_dim, dim, bias=False)
   139→    )
   140→    up_proj = (
   141→        nn.Linear(dim, hidden_dim, bias=False)
   142→        if not quantize_base
   143→        else FrozenNF4Linear(dim, hidden_dim, bias=False)
   144→    )
   145→    return FeedForward(gate_proj=gate_proj, down_proj=down_proj, up_proj=up_proj)

   151→def lora_llama2(
   152→    lora_attn_modules: List[LORA_ATTN_MODULES],
   153→    apply_lora_to_mlp: bool = False,
   154→    apply_lora_to_output: bool = False,
   155→    *,
   156→    # llama2 args
   157→    vocab_size: int,
   158→    num_layers: int,
   159→    num_heads: int,
   160→    num_kv_heads: int,
   161→    embed_dim: int,
   162→    max_seq_len: int,
   163→    intermediate_dim: Optional[int] = None,
   164→    attn_dropout: float = 0.0,
   165→    norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
   166→    # LoRA args
   167→    lora_rank: int,
   168→    lora_alpha: float,
   169→    lora_dropout: float = 0.0,
   170→    use_dora: bool = False,
   171→    # Quantization args
   172→    quantize_base: bool = False,
   173→) -> TransformerDecoder:
   174→    """
   175→    Return a version of Llama2 (an instance of :func:`~torchtune.modules.TransformerDecoder`)
   176→    with LoRA applied based on the passed in configuration.
   177→
   178→    Args:
   179→        lora_attn_modules (List[LORA_ATTN_MODULES]): list of which linear layers
   180→            LoRA should be applied to in each self-attention block. Options are
   181→            ``{"q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "output_proj"}``.
   182→        apply_lora_to_mlp (bool): whether to apply LoRA to the MLP in each transformer layer.
   183→            Default: False
   184→        apply_lora_to_output (bool): whether to apply LoRA to the model's final output projection.
   185→            Default: False
   186→        vocab_size (int): number of tokens in vocabulary.
   187→        num_layers (int): number of layers in the transformer decoder.
   188→        num_heads (int): number of query heads. For MHA this is also the
   189→            number of heads for key and value
   190→        num_kv_heads (int): number of key and value heads. User should ensure
   191→            `num_heads` % `num_kv_heads` == 0. For standard MHA set `num_kv_heads` == `num_heads`,
   192→            for GQA `num_kv_heads` < `num_heads`, and for MQA set `num_kv_heads` == 1.
   193→        embed_dim (int): embedding dimension for self-attention
   194→        max_seq_len (int): maximum sequence length the model will be run with, as used
   195→            by :func:`~torchtune.modules.KVCache`
   196→        attn_dropout (float): dropout value passed onto scaled_dot_product_attention.
   197→            Default: 0.0
   198→        intermediate_dim (Optional[int]): intermediate dimension for MLP. If not specified,
   199→            this is computed using :func:`~torchtune.modules.scale_hidden_dim_for_mlp`
   200→        norm_eps (float): epsilon in RMS norms.
   201→        lora_rank (int): rank of each low-rank approximation
   202→        lora_alpha (float): scaling factor for the low-rank approximation
   203→        lora_dropout (float): LoRA dropout probability. Default: 0.0
   204→        use_dora (bool): Decompose the LoRA weight into magnitude and direction, as
   205→            introduced in "DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09353).
   206→        quantize_base: (bool): Whether to quantize base model weights or not. Only applied to base
   207→            weights within linear layers LoRA is applied to. The final output linear projection is not
   208→            supported for quantization currently.
   209→
   210→    Returns:
   211→        TransformerDecoder: Instantiation of Llama2 model with LoRA applied to
   212→        a subset of the attention projections in each layer.
   213→
   214→    """
   215→
   216→    self_attn = lora_llama2_self_attention(
   217→        lora_modules=lora_attn_modules,
   218→        embed_dim=embed_dim,
   219→        num_heads=num_heads,
   220→        num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
   221→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   222→        attn_dropout=attn_dropout,
   223→        lora_rank=lora_rank,
   224→        lora_alpha=lora_alpha,
   225→        lora_dropout=lora_dropout,
   226→        use_dora=use_dora,
   227→        quantize_base=quantize_base,
   228→    )
   229→
   230→    hidden_dim = (
   231→        intermediate_dim if intermediate_dim else scale_hidden_dim_for_mlp(embed_dim)
   232→    )
   233→    if apply_lora_to_mlp:
   234→        mlp = lora_llama2_mlp(
   235→            dim=embed_dim,
   236→            hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
   237→            lora_rank=lora_rank,
   238→            lora_alpha=lora_alpha,
   239→            quantize_base=quantize_base,
   240→            use_dora=use_dora,
   241→            lora_dropout=lora_dropout,
   242→        )
   243→    else:
   244→        mlp = llama2_mlp(
   245→            dim=embed_dim, hidden_dim=hidden_dim, quantize_base=quantize_base
   246→        )
   247→
   248→    layer = TransformerSelfAttentionLayer(
   249→        attn=self_attn,
   250→        mlp=mlp,
   251→        sa_norm=RMSNorm(dim=embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   252→        mlp_norm=RMSNorm(dim=embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   253→    )
   254→
   255→    tok_embeddings = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
   256→
   257→    # TODO: quantize_base is not applied to final output_proj currently.
   258→    adapter_cls = DoRALinear if use_dora else LoRALinear
   259→    output_proj = (
   260→        adapter_cls(
   261→            embed_dim,
   262→            vocab_size,
   263→            rank=lora_rank,
   264→            alpha=lora_alpha,
   265→            dropout=lora_dropout,
   266→        )
   267→        if apply_lora_to_output
   268→        else nn.Linear(embed_dim, vocab_size, bias=False)
   269→    )
   270→    model = TransformerDecoder(
   271→        tok_embeddings=tok_embeddings,
   272→        layers=layer,
   273→        num_layers=num_layers,
   274→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   275→        num_heads=num_heads,
   276→        head_dim=(embed_dim // num_heads),
   277→        norm=RMSNorm(embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   278→        output=output_proj,
   279→    )
   280→
   281→    if quantize_base:
   282→        # For QLoRA, we reparametrize 4-bit tensors to higher precision, and offload to CPU on the fly
   283→        # so as to not increase peak memory
   284→        # TODO this is clowny, figure out a better way to get what precision the rest
   285→        # of the model is in
   286→        _register_reparametrize_state_dict_hooks(model, dtype=tok_embeddings.weight.dtype)
   287→
   288→    return model

   291→def lora_llama2_self_attention(
   292→    lora_modules: List[LORA_ATTN_MODULES],
   293→    *,
   294→    # MultiHeadAttention args
   295→    embed_dim: int,
   296→    num_heads: int,
   297→    num_kv_heads: int,
   298→    max_seq_len: int,
   299→    attn_dropout: float = 0.0,
   300→    # LoRA args
   301→    lora_rank: int,
   302→    lora_alpha: float,
   303→    lora_dropout: float = 0.0,
   304→    use_dora: bool = False,
   305→    quantize_base: bool = False,
   306→) -> MultiHeadAttention:
   307→    """
   308→    Return an instance of :func:`~torchtune.modules.MultiHeadAttention` with LoRA
   309→    applied to a subset of its linear layers
   310→
   311→    Args:
   312→        lora_modules (List[LORA_ATTN_MODULES]): list of which linear layers
   313→            LoRA should be applied to. Options are ``{"q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj",
   314→            "output_proj"}``.
   315→        embed_dim (int): embedding dimension for self-attention
   316→        num_heads (int): number of query heads. For MHA this is also the
   317→            number of heads for key and value
   318→        num_kv_heads (int): number of key and value heads. User should ensure
   319→            `num_heads` % `num_kv_heads` == 0. For standard MHA set `num_kv_heads` == `num_heads`,
   320→            for GQA `num_kv_heads` < `num_heads`, and for MQA set `num_kv_heads` == 1.
   321→        max_seq_len (int): maximum sequence length the model will be run with, as used
   322→            by :func:`~torchtune.modules.KVCache`
   323→        attn_dropout (float): dropout value passed onto scaled_dot_product_attention.
   324→            Default: 0.0
   325→        lora_rank (int): rank of each low-rank approximation
   326→        lora_alpha (float): scaling factor for the low-rank approximation
   327→        lora_dropout (float): LoRA dropout probability. Default: 0.0
   328→        use_dora (bool): Decompose the LoRA weight into magnitude and direction, as
   329→            introduced in "DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09353).
   330→        quantize_base (bool): Whether to quantize base model parameters for linear layers
   331→            LoRA is being applied to. Default is ``False``.
   332→
   333→    Returns:
   334→        MultiHeadAttention: instantiation of self-attention module with LoRA
   335→        applied to a subset of Q, K, V, output projections.
   336→
   337→    Raises:
   338→        ValueError: If lora_modules arg is an empty list
   339→    """
   340→    if not lora_modules:
   341→        raise ValueError(
   342→            f"Must pass one or more of {LORA_ATTN_MODULES} as lora_modules"
   343→        )
   344→
   345→    head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
   346→    num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads if num_kv_heads else num_heads
   347→    adapter_cls = DoRALinear if use_dora else LoRALinear
   348→    q_proj = (
   349→        adapter_cls(
   350→            embed_dim,
   351→            num_heads * head_dim,
   352→            rank=lora_rank,
   353→            alpha=lora_alpha,
   354→            dropout=lora_dropout,
   355→            quantize_base=quantize_base,
   356→        )
   357→        if "q_proj" in lora_modules
   358→        else (
   359→            nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
   360→            if not quantize_base
   361→            else FrozenNF4Linear(embed_dim, num_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
   362→        )
   363→    )
   364→    k_proj = (
   365→        adapter_cls(
   366→            embed_dim,
   367→            num_kv_heads * head_dim,
   368→            rank=lora_rank,
   369→            alpha=lora_alpha,
   370→            dropout=lora_dropout,
   371→            quantize_base=quantize_base,
   372→        )
   373→        if "k_proj" in lora_modules
   374→        else (
   375→            nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
   376→            if not quantize_base
   377→            else FrozenNF4Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
   378→        )
   379→    )
   380→    v_proj = (
   381→        adapter_cls(
   382→            embed_dim,
   383→            num_kv_heads * head_dim,
   384→            rank=lora_rank,
   385→            alpha=lora_alpha,
   386→            dropout=lora_dropout,
   387→            quantize_base=quantize_base,
   388→        )
   389→        if "v_proj" in lora_modules
   390→        else (
   391→            nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
   392→            if not quantize_base
   393→            else FrozenNF4Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
   394→        )
   395→    )
   396→    output_proj = (
   397→        adapter_cls(
   398→            embed_dim,
   399→            embed_dim,
   400→            rank=lora_rank,
   401→            alpha=lora_alpha,
   402→            dropout=lora_dropout,
   403→            quantize_base=quantize_base,
   404→        )
   405→        if "output_proj" in lora_modules
   406→        else (
   407→            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim, bias=False)
   408→            if not quantize_base
   409→            else FrozenNF4Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim, bias=False)
   410→        )
   411→    )
   412→    rope = RotaryPositionalEmbeddings(dim=head_dim, max_seq_len=max_seq_len)
   413→    self_attn = MultiHeadAttention(
   414→        embed_dim=embed_dim,
   415→        num_heads=num_heads,
   416→        num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
   417→        head_dim=head_dim,
   418→        q_proj=q_proj,
   419→        k_proj=k_proj,
   420→        v_proj=v_proj,
   421→        output_proj=output_proj,
   422→        pos_embeddings=rope,
   423→        kv_cache=None,
   424→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   425→        attn_dropout=attn_dropout,
   426→    )
   427→    return self_attn
   428→
   429→
   430→def lora_llama2_mlp(
   431→    *,
   432→    dim: int,
   433→    hidden_dim: int,
   434→    lora_rank: int,
   435→    lora_alpha: float,
   436→    lora_dropout: float = 0.0,
   437→    use_dora: bool = False,
   438→    quantize_base: bool = False,
   439→) -> FeedForward:
   440→    adapter_cls = DoRALinear if use_dora else LoRALinear
   441→    gate_proj = adapter_cls(
   442→        in_dim=dim,
   443→        out_dim=hidden_dim,
   444→        rank=lora_rank,
   445→        alpha=lora_alpha,
   446→        dropout=lora_dropout,
   447→        quantize_base=quantize_base,
   448→    )
   449→    down_proj = adapter_cls(
   450→        in_dim=hidden_dim,
   451→        out_dim=dim,
   452→        rank=lora_rank,
   453→        alpha=lora_alpha,
   454→        dropout=lora_dropout,
   455→        quantize_base=quantize_base,
   456→    )
   457→    up_proj = adapter_cls(
   458→        in_dim=dim,
   459→        out_dim=hidden_dim,
   460→        rank=lora_rank,
   461→        alpha=lora_alpha,
   462→        dropout=lora_dropout,
   463→        quantize_base=quantize_base,
   464    )
   465→    return FeedForward(
   466→        gate_proj=gate_proj,
   467→        down_proj=down_proj,
   468→        up_proj=up_proj,
   469→    )

   475→def llama2_classifier(
   476→    num_classes: int,
   477→    *,
   478→    vocab_size: int,
   479→    num_layers: int,
   480→    num_heads: int,
   481→    num_kv_heads: int,
   482→    embed_dim: int,
   483→    max_seq_len: int,
   484→    attn_dropout: float = 0.0,
   485→    intermediate_dim: Optional[int] = None,
   486→    norm_eps: float = 1e-5,
   487→) -> TransformerDecoder:
   488→    """
   489→    Build a base Llama2 model with the final projection replaced with a classification layer.
   490→
   491→    Args:
   492→        num_classes (int): number of classes for classification.
   493→        vocab_size (int): number of tokens in vocabulary.
   494→        num_layers (int): number of layers in the transformer decoder.
   495→        num_heads (int): number of query heads. For MHA this is also the
   496→            number of heads for key and value
   497→        num_kv_heads (int): number of key and value heads. If specified,
   498→            user should ensure `num_heads` % `num_kv_heads` == 0. Default value is
   499→            `None`, in which case this is the same as MHA
   500→        embed_dim (int): embedding dimension for self-attention
   501→        max_seq_len (int): maximum sequence length the model will be run with, as used
   502→            by :func:`~torchtune.modules.KVCache`
   503→        attn_dropout (float): dropout value passed onto scaled_dot_product_attention.
   504→            Default: 0.0
   505→        intermediate_dim (Optional[int]): intermediate dimension for MLP. If not specified,
   506→            this is computed using :func:`~torchtune.modules.scale_hidden_dim_for_mlp`
   507→        norm_eps (float): epsilon in RMS norms.
   508→
   509→    Returns:
   510→        TransformerDecoder: Instantiation of Llama2 model.
   511→    """
   512→    head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
   513→    num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads if num_kv_heads else num_heads
   514→
   515→    rope = RotaryPositionalEmbeddings(dim=head_dim, max_seq_len=max_seq_len)
   516→    self_attn = MultiHeadAttention(
   517→        embed_dim=embed_dim,
   518→        num_heads=num_heads,
   519→        num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
   520→        head_dim=head_dim,
   521→        q_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_heads * head_dim, bias=False),
   522→        k_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False),
   523→        v_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False),
   524→        output_proj=nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim, bias=False),
   525→        pos_embeddings=rope,
   526→        kv_cache=None,
   527→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   528→        attn_dropout=attn_dropout,
   529→    )
   530→    hidden_dim = (
   531→        intermediate_dim if intermediate_dim else scale_hidden_dim_for_mlp(embed_dim)
   532→    )
   533→    mlp = llama2_mlp(dim=embed_dim, hidden_dim=hidden_dim)
   534→    layer = TransformerSelfAttentionLayer(
   535→        attn=self_attn,
   536→        mlp=mlp,
   537→        sa_norm=RMSNorm(dim=embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   538→        mlp_norm=RMSNorm(dim=embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   539→    )
   540→    tok_embeddings = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
   541→    output_proj = nn.Linear(embed_dim, num_classes, bias=False)
   542→    return TransformerDecoder(
   543→        tok_embeddings=tok_embeddings,
   544→        layers=layer,
   545→        num_layers=num_layers,
   546→        max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
   547→        num_heads=num_heads,
   548→        head_dim=head_dim,
   549→        norm=RMSNorm(embed_dim, eps=norm_eps),
   550→        output=output_proj,
   551→    )

        """

        BEFORE initialize_dora_magnitude is called, and that no params remain on meta.
        """
        from omegaconf import OmegaConf
        from torchtune import config as tt_config, training
        from torchtune.modules.peft import DoRALinear, LoRALinear, load_dora_magnitudes

        # Build a tiny DoRA-enabled model on the meta device
        with training.set_default_dtype(torch.float32), torch.device("meta"):
            model = tt_config.instantiate(
                OmegaConf.from_dotlist(MODEL_TEST_CONFIGS["llama2_dora"]).model
            )

        # Initialize LoRA params (lora_a/lora_b) and any RoPE buffers off meta
        for m in model.modules():
            if isinstance(m, (LoRALinear, DoRALinear)):
                m.lora_a.to_empty(device="cpu")
                m.lora_b.to_empty(device="cpu")
                m.initialize_parameters()
            if hasattr(m, "rope_init"):
                m.rope_init()

        # Construct a dummy base state dict (non-adapter params only) to materialize base weights
        from torchtune.modules.peft import get_adapter_params

        adapter_param_names = set(get_adapter_params(model).keys())
        base_sd = {}
        for k, v in model.state_dict().items():
            if k in adapter_param_names:
                continue
            shape = v.shape
            dtype = v.dtype if not v.is_meta else torch.float32
            base_sd[k] = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=dtype)

        # Materialize base weights using the same utility the recipe uses
        training.load_from_full_model_state_dict(
            model, base_sd, device=torch.device("cpu"), is_rank_zero=True, cpu_offload=False
        )

        # Now materialize DoRA magnitudes OFF meta before initialization
        load_dora_magnitudes(model)
        for m in model.modules():
            if hasattr(m, "initialize_dora_magnitude"):
                m.initialize_dora_magnitude()

        # Validate no params or buffers remain on meta
        training.validate_no_params_on_meta_device(model)

   161→class _DoraReference(nn.Module):
   162→    """
   163→    DoRA linear layer reference.
   164→
   165→    Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09353
   166→
   167→    Based on the code from:
   168→    https://github.com/huggingface/peft/blob/main/src/peft/tuners/lora/layer.py

   172→    https://github.com/huggingface/peft/pull/1474

   175→    def __init__(
   176→        self,
   177→        dtype: torch.dtype,
   178→        in_dim: int,
   179→        out_dim: int,
   180→        rank: int,
   181→        alpha: float,
   182→        dropout: float = 0.0,
   183→        use_bias: bool = False,
   184→        quantize_base: bool = False,
   185→        use_dora: bool = True,

   188→        self.use_bias = use_bias
   189→        self.quantize_base = quantize_base
   190→        self.use_dora = use_dora

   194→        )

   196→        bias = None
   197→        if use_bias:
   198→            if quantize_base:
   199→                raise NotImplementedError()
   200→            bias = linear.bias
   201→        self.register_parameter("weight", nn.Parameter(weight))
   202→        self.register_parameter(
   203→            "bias", nn.Parameter(bias) if bias is not None else None
   204→        )
   205→
   206→        self.lora_a = nn.Linear(in_dim, rank, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
   207→        self.lora_b = nn.Linear(rank, out_dim, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
   208→        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.lora_a.weight, a=math.sqrt(5))
   209→        nn.init.zeros_(self.lora_b.weight)
   210→        self.scaling = alpha / rank
   211→        if use_dora:
   212→            self.lora_magnitude = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_dim, dtype=dtype))
   213→        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(p=dropout)
   214→
   215→    def initialize_dora(self):
   216→        weight = self.weight.to(self.lora_a.weight.dtype)
   217→        lora_weight = self.lora_b.weight @ self.lora_a.weight
   218→        weight_norm = self._get_weight_norm(weight, lora_weight)
   219→        self.lora_magnitude = nn.Parameter(weight_norm, requires_grad=True)
   220→
   221→    def forward(self, x):
   222→        result = self._base_forward(x)
   223→        torch_result_dtype = result.dtype
   224→        x = x.to(self.lora_a.weight.dtype)
   225→        if not self.use_dora:
   226→            result = result + self.lora_b(self.lora_a(self.dropout(x))) * self.scaling
   227→        else:
   228→            x = self.dropout(x)
   229→            result = result + self._dora_forward(x)
   230→        result = result.to(torch_result_dtype)
   231→        print("result mean", result.mean())
   232→        return result
   233→
   234→    def _base_forward(self, x):
   235→        if self.quantize_base:
   236→            return linear_nf4(input=x, weight=self.weight)
   237→        return F.linear(x, self.weight, self.bias)
   238→
   239→    def _dora_forward(self, x):
   240→        lora_result = self.lora_b(self.lora_a(x))
   241→        x_eye = torch.eye(
   242→            self.lora_a.weight.shape[1], device=self.lora_a.weight.device, dtype=x.dtype
   243→        )
   244→        lora_weight = self.lora_b(self.lora_a(x_eye)).T
   245→
   246→        magnitude = self.lora_magnitude
   247→        weight = self.weight.to(x.dtype)
   248→        weight_norm = self._get_weight_norm(weight, lora_weight.detach())
   249→        weight_norm = weight_norm.detach()
   250→        mag_norm_scale = (magnitude / weight_norm).view(1, -1)
   251→        result_dora = (mag_norm_scale - 1) * (
   252→            F.linear(x, weight)
   253→        ) + mag_norm_scale * lora_result * self.scaling
   254→        return result_dora
   255→
   256→    def _get_weight_norm(self, weight, lora_weight):
   257→        weight = weight + self.scaling * lora_weight
   258→        weight_norm = torch.linalg.norm(weight, dim=1).to(weight.dtype)
   259→        return weight_norm

   215→
   216→            # on mismatch, warn the user and prevent the override
   217→            if self.seed != ckpt_dict[training.SEED_KEY]:
   218→                warn(
   219→                    message=(
   220→                        "Config value for seed does not match the checkpoint value, "
   221→                        f"using the checkpoint value: {ckpt_dict[training.SEED_KEY]}"
   222→                    )
   223→                )
   224→                self.seed = ckpt_dict[training.SEED_KEY]
   225→            if self.max_steps_per_epoch != ckpt_dict[training.MAX_STEPS_KEY]:
   226→                warn(
   227→                    message=(
   228→                        "Config value for max_steps_per_epoch does not match the checkpoint value, "
   229→                        f"using the checkpoint value: {ckpt_dict[training.MAX_STEPS_KEY]}"
   230→                    )
   231→                )
   232→                self.max_steps_per_epoch = ckpt_dict[training.MAX_STEPS_KEY]
   233→
   234→            # on mismatch, warn the user but allow the override
   235→            if self.total_epochs != ckpt_dict[training.TOTAL_EPOCHS_KEY]:
   236→                warn(
   237→                    message=(
   238→                        "Config value for total_epochs does not match the checkpoint value, "
   239→                        f"using the config value: {self.total_epochs}"
   240→                    )
   241→                )
   242→
   243→        except KeyError as e:
   244→            raise KeyError(
   245→                "Checkpoint does not contain the required keys needed for updating recipe state. "
   246→                "Are you sure you passed in the right recipe checkpoint?"
   247→            ) from e
   248→
   249→    def setup(self, cfg: DictConfig) -> None:
   250→        """
   251→        Setup the recipe state. This includes recipe state (if resume_from_checkpoint is True),
   252→        model, tokenizer, loss, optimizer, learning rate scheduler, sampler, and dataloader.
   253→        """
   254→        if self._is_rank_zero:
   255→            self._metric_logger = config.instantiate(cfg.metric_logger)
   256→
   257→            # log config with parameter override
   258→            self._metric_logger.log_config(cfg)
   259→
   260→        utils.log_rank_zero(log, "metric logger is initialized.")
   261→
   262→        checkpoint_dict = self.load_checkpoint(cfg_checkpointer=cfg.checkpointer)
   263→
   264→        self._model = self._setup_model(
   265→            cfg_model=cfg.model,
   266→            enable_activation_checkpointing=cfg.enable_activation_checkpointing,
   267→            enable_activation_offloading=self._enable_activation_offloading,
   268→            custom_sharded_layers=cfg.get("custom_sharded_layers", None),
   269→            fsdp_cpu_offload=cfg.get("fsdp_cpu_offload", False),
   270→            reshard_after_forward=cfg.get("fsdp_reshard_after_forward", True),
   271→            base_model_state_dict=checkpoint_dict[training.MODEL_KEY],
   272→            lora_weights_state_dict=(
   273→                checkpoint_dict[training.ADAPTER_KEY]
   274→                if self._resume_from_checkpoint
   275→                else None
   276→            ),
   277→        )
   278→        self._tokenizer = config.instantiate(cfg.tokenizer)
   279→
   280→        self._optimizer = self._setup_optimizer(
   281→            cfg_optimizer=cfg.optimizer,
   282→            opt_state_dict=(
   283→                checkpoint_dict[training.OPT_KEY]
   284→                if self._resume_from_checkpoint
   285→                else None
   286→            ),
   287→        )
   288→
   289→        self._loss_fn = config.instantiate(cfg.loss)
   290→
   291→        utils.log_rank_zero(log, "Loss is initialized.")
   292→
   293→        # sampler and dataloader depend on the tokenizer and loss_fn and should be
   294→        # setup after all of these are setup
   295→        self._sampler, self._dataloader = self._setup_data(
   296→            cfg_dataset=cfg.dataset,
   297→            shuffle=cfg.shuffle,
   298→            batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
   299→        )
   300→
   301→        # Finally update the recipe state which can only be correctly set after all of the
   302→        # other components have been initialized and updated.
   303→
   304→        # Number of training steps in each epoch depends on the number of batches produced
   305→        # by the dataloader and the max_steps_per_epoch param set by the user and is used
   306→        # for logging and tracking training state. This should be computed after the dataloader
   307→        # has been setup
   308→        self._steps_per_epoch = (
   309→            len(self._dataloader) // self._gradient_accumulation_steps
   310→        )
   311→        if (
   312→            self.max_steps_per_epoch is not None
   313→            and self.max_steps_per_epoch < self._steps_per_epoch
   314→        ):
   315→            self._steps_per_epoch = self.max_steps_per_epoch
   316→        self.global_step = self.epochs_run * self._steps_per_epoch
   317→
   318→        # Learning rate scheduler can only be set up after number of steps
   319→        # has been computed
   320→        self._lr_scheduler = self._setup_lr_scheduler(
   321→            cfg_lr_scheduler=cfg.lr_scheduler,
   322→            num_training_steps=self.total_epochs * self._steps_per_epoch,
   323→            last_epoch=self.global_step - 1,
   324→        )

   326→    def _setup_model(
   327→        self,
   328→        cfg_model: DictConfig,
   329→        enable_activation_checkpointing: bool,
   330→        enable_activation_offloading: bool,
   331→        fsdp_cpu_offload: bool,
   332→        reshard_after_forward: bool,
   333→        base_model_state_dict: Dict[str, Any],
   334→        custom_sharded_layers: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   335→        lora_weights_state_dict: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   336→    ) -> nn.Module:
   337→        """
   338→        Model initialization has some important considerations:
   339→           a. To minimize GPU peak memory, we initialize the model on meta device with
   340→              the right dtype
   341→           b. All ranks calls ``load_state_dict`` without peaking CPU RAMs since
   342→              full state dicts are loaded with ``torch.load(mmap=True)``
   343→           c. We register (pre-)forward hooks with ``fully_shard`` instead of wrapping `nn.Module`
   344→        """
   345→        self._lora_rank = cfg_model.lora_rank
   346→        self._lora_alpha = cfg_model.lora_alpha
   347→        self._lora_attn_modules = list(cfg_model.lora_attn_modules)
   348→        self._apply_lora_to_mlp = cfg_model.apply_lora_to_mlp
   349→        self._apply_lora_to_output = getattr(cfg_model, "apply_lora_to_output", False)
   350→
   351→        init_start = time.perf_counter()
   352→
   353→        utils.log_rank_zero(
   354→            log,
   355→            "FSDP is enabled. Instantiating model and loading checkpoint on Rank 0 ...",
   356→        )
   357→
   358→        with training.set_default_dtype(self._dtype), torch.device("meta"):
   359→            model = config.instantiate(cfg_model)
   360→
   361→        self.adapter_params = get_adapter_params(model)
   362→        set_trainable_params(model, self.adapter_params)
   363→
   364→        if enable_activation_checkpointing:
   365→            training.set_activation_checkpointing(
   366→                model, auto_wrap_policy={modules.TransformerSelfAttentionLayer}
   367→            )
   368→
   369→        # For FSDP sharding
   370→        fsdp_shard_conditions = [
   371→            partial(
   372→                training.get_shard_conditions,
   373→                names_to_match=custom_sharded_layers,
   374→            )
   375→        ]
   376→        training.shard_model(
   377→            model=model,
   378→            shard_conditions=fsdp_shard_conditions,
   379→            cpu_offload=fsdp_cpu_offload,
   380→            reshard_after_forward=reshard_after_forward,
   381→        )
   382→
   383→        if lora_weights_state_dict:
   384→            lora_missing, lora_unexpected = training.load_from_full_model_state_dict(
   385→                model,
   386→                lora_weights_state_dict,
   387→                self._device,
   388→                self._is_rank_zero,
   389→                cpu_offload=fsdp_cpu_offload,
   390→            )
   391→        else:
   392→            lora_missing, lora_unexpected = None, None
   393→
   394→        # Initialize LoRA params and RoPE buffers
   395→        with training.set_default_dtype(self._dtype), self._device:
   396→            lora_device = "cpu" if fsdp_cpu_offload else self._device
   397→            for m in model.modules():
   398→                if (
   399→                    isinstance(m, LoRALinear) or isinstance(m, DoRALinear)
   400→                ) and not lora_weights_state_dict:
   401→                    # lora may not be covered in state dict
   402→                    # if finetune for the 1st time
   403→                    m.lora_a.to_empty(device=lora_device)
   404→                    m.lora_b.to_empty(device=lora_device)
   405→                    m.initialize_parameters()
   406→                # RoPE is not covered in state dict
   407→                if hasattr(m, "rope_init"):
   408→                    m.rope_init()
   409→
   410→        base_missing, base_unexpected = training.load_from_full_model_state_dict(
   411→            model,
   412→            base_model_state_dict,
   413→            self._device,
   414→            self._is_rank_zero,
   415→            cpu_offload=fsdp_cpu_offload,
   416→        )
   417→        is_dora = False
   418→        for m in model.modules():
   419→            if hasattr(m, "initialize_dora_magnitude"):
   420→                is_dora = True
   421→                m.initialize_dora_magnitude()
   422→        if is_dora:
   423→            load_dora_magnitudes(model)
   424→        validate_missing_and_unexpected_for_lora(
   425→            lora_attn_modules=self._lora_attn_modules,
   426→            apply_lora_to_mlp=self._apply_lora_to_mlp,
   427→            apply_lora_to_output=self._apply_lora_to_output,
   428→            base_missing=base_missing,
   429→            base_unexpected=base_unexpected,
   430→            lora_missing=lora_missing,
   431→            lora_unexpected=lora_unexpected,
   432→        )
   433→        # Ensure no params and buffers are on meta device
   434→
   435→        # activation offloading
   436→        self.activations_handling_ctx = training.get_act_offloading_ctx_manager(
   437→            model, enable_activation_offloading
   438→        )
   439→
   440→        training.validate_no_params_on_meta_device(model)
   441→        utils.log_rank_zero(
   442→            log,
   443→            f"Instantiating model and loading checkpoint took {time.perf_counter() - init_start:.2f} secs",
   444→        )
   445→        if self._is_rank_zero:
   446→            memory_stats = training.get_memory_stats(device=self._device)
   447→            training.log_memory_stats(memory_stats)
   448→
   449→        # synchronize before training begins
   450→        torch.distributed.barrier()
   451→
   452→        return model

   484→    def _setup_data(
   485→        self,
   486→        cfg_dataset: DictConfig,
   487→        shuffle: bool,
   488→        batch_size: int,
   489→    ) -> Tuple[DistributedSampler, DataLoader]:
   490→        """
   491→        All data related setup happens here. Currently this recipe only supports the
   492→        DistributedSamplers with Map-style Datasets which fit into memory. Other samplers,
   493→        iterable datasets and streaming datasets are not supported.
   494→        """
   495→        world_size, rank = training.get_world_size_and_rank()
   496→
   497→        if isinstance(cfg_dataset, ListConfig):
   498→            datasets = [
   499→                config.instantiate(single_cfg_dataset, tokenizer=self._tokenizer)
   500→                for single_cfg_dataset in cfg_dataset
   501→            ]
   502→            ds = ConcatDataset(datasets=datasets)
   503→        else:
   504→            ds = config.instantiate(cfg_dataset, tokenizer=self._tokenizer)
   505→
   506→        sampler = DistributedSampler(
   507→            ds, num_replicas=world_size, rank=rank, shuffle=shuffle, seed=0
   508→        )
   509→
   510→        dataloader = DataLoader(
   511→            dataset=ds,
   512→            batch_size=batch_size,
   513→            sampler=sampler,
   514→            # dropping last avoids shape issues with compile + flex attention
   515→            drop_last=True,
   516→            collate_fn=partial(
   517→                padded_collate_dpo,
   518→                padding_idx=self._tokenizer.pad_id,
   519→                ignore_idx=CROSS_ENTROPY_IGNORE_IDX,
   520→            ),
   521→        )
   522→
   523→        utils.log_rank_zero(log, "Dataset and Sampler are initialized.")
   524→
   525→        return sampler, dataloader

   527→    def save_checkpoint(
   528→        self,
   529→        epoch: int,
   530→    ) -> None:
   531→        """
   532→        Checkpoint the state of the recipe. The constructed checkpoint state dict
   533→        contains the following information:
   534→        - Merged weights with key MODEL_KEY
   535→        - Adapter weights with key ADAPTER_KEY
   536→        - Relevant recipe state if training is not complete
   537→        - If the `self._save_adapter_weights_only` option is True, the checkpointer will save only the adapter weights
   538→
   539→        Checkpointer will save the merged weights, adapter weights and recipe state in
   540→        different checkpoint files. To correctly resume from training, the adapter weights
   541→        and recipe state must be provided along with the base model weights."""
   542→        # final dict passed onto the checkpointer
   543→        checkpoint_dict = {}
   544→
   545→        intermediate_checkpoint = epoch + 1 < self.total_epochs
   546→        # To prevent GPU memory from spiking during checkpoint save,
   547→        # we consolidate the full model and optim state dicts on CPU for rank 0
   548→        state_dict = self._model.state_dict()
   549→        if self._save_adapter_weights_only:
   550→            state_dict = get_adapter_state_dict(state_dict, device=None)
   551→
   552→        cpu_state_dict = training.gather_cpu_state_dict(
   553→            state_dict,
   554→            self._is_rank_zero,
   555→            device=self._device,
   556→        )
   557→        if intermediate_checkpoint:
   558→            opt_state_dict = training.get_full_optimizer_state_dict(
   559→                self._optimizer,
   560→                self._is_rank_zero,
   561→                device=self._device,
   562→            )
   563→        else:
   564→            opt_state_dict = None
   565→
   566→        # Now that we have the model and opt state dict, create the actual checkpoint dict
   567→        # to be sent to the checkpointer and ultimately written to file
   568→        if self._is_rank_zero:
   569→            if self._save_adapter_weights_only:
   570→                adapter_state_dict = cpu_state_dict
   571→            else:
   572→                # Filter out the adapter keys and weights from the model state dict. These will
   573→                # be saved separately
   574→                adapter_state_dict = get_adapter_state_dict(cpu_state_dict)
   575→
   576→                # merge the adapter weights and base weights to create the model checkpoint
   577→                merged_state_dict = get_merged_lora_ckpt(
   578→                    cpu_state_dict,
   579→                    rank=self._lora_rank,
   580→                    alpha=self._lora_alpha,
   581→                )
   582→                checkpoint_dict.update({training.MODEL_KEY: merged_state_dict})
   583→            checkpoint_dict.update({training.ADAPTER_KEY: adapter_state_dict})
   584→
   585→            # if training is in-progress, checkpoint the optimizer state and recipe state
   586→            # as well.
   587→            if intermediate_checkpoint:
   588→                checkpoint_dict.update(
   589→                    {
   590→                        training.OPT_KEY: opt_state_dict,
   591→                        training.SEED_KEY: self.seed,
   592→                        training.EPOCHS_KEY: self.epochs_run,
   593→                        training.TOTAL_EPOCHS_KEY: self.total_epochs,
   594→                        training.MAX_STEPS_KEY: self.max_steps_per_epoch,
   595→                    }
   596→                )
   597→
   598→            self._checkpointer.save_checkpoint(
   599→                checkpoint_dict,
   600→                epoch=epoch,
   601→                intermediate_checkpoint=intermediate_checkpoint,
   602→                adapter_only=self._save_adapter_weights_only,
   603→            )
   604→
   605→    def concatenated_forward(
   606→        self, model: nn.Module, batch: Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
   607→    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   608→        """
   609→        Run forward pass of the model with chosen and rejected samples concatenated.
   610→
   611→        Args:
   612→            model (nn.Module): The model to be used for the forward pass.
   613→            batch (Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]): Tuple of input_ids and labels.
   614→
   615→        Returns:
   616→            Tuple of chosen log probs, rejected log probs, chosen logits, rejected logits.
   617→        """
   618→        concatenated_input_ids, concatenated_labels = batch
   619→        concatenated_input_ids = concatenated_input_ids.to(self._device)
   620→        concatenated_labels = concatenated_labels.to(self._device)
   621→
   622→        # formed by concatenating an equal number of "chosen" and "rejected".
   623→        len_chosen = concatenated_input_ids.shape[0] // 2
   624→
   625→        with self.activations_handling_ctx:
   626→            all_logits = model(concatenated_input_ids)
   627→
   628→        all_log_probs = rlhf.get_batch_log_probs(all_logits, concatenated_labels)
   629→
   630→        chosen_log_probs = all_log_probs[:len_chosen]
   631→        rejected_log_probs = all_log_probs[len_chosen:]
   632→
   633→        chosen_logits = all_logits[:len_chosen]
   634→        rejected_logits = all_logits[len_chosen:]
   635→
   636→        return (chosen_log_probs, rejected_log_probs, chosen_logits, rejected_logits)
   637→
   638→    def train(self) -> None:
   639→        """
   640→        The core training loop.
   641→        """
   642→        # clean up before training begins
   643→        training.cleanup_before_training()
   644→
   645→        _, rank = training.get_world_size_and_rank()
   646→
   647→        # zero out the gradients before starting training
   648→        self._optimizer.zero_grad()
   649→
   650→        # Initialize tokens count and running loss (for grad accumulation)
   651→        t0 = time.perf_counter()
   652→        running_loss = 0
   653→        num_tokens = 0
   654→
   655→        # self.epochs_run should be non-zero when we're resuming from a checkpoint
   656→        for curr_epoch in range(self.epochs_run, self.total_epochs):
   657→
   658→            # Update the sampler to ensure data is correctly shuffled across epochs
   659→            # in case shuffle is True
   660→            self._sampler.set_epoch(curr_epoch)
   661→
   662→            pbar = tqdm(total=self._steps_per_epoch, disable=not (rank == 0))
   663→            for idx, batch in enumerate(self._dataloader):
   664→                if (
   665→                    self.max_steps_per_epoch is not None
   666→                    and (idx // self._gradient_accumulation_steps)
   667→                    == self.max_steps_per_epoch
   668→                ):
   669→                    break
   670→
   671→                # batch is input_ids, labels
   672→                num_tokens += batch[0].numel()
   673→
   674→                (
   675→                    policy_chosen_log_probs,
   676→                    policy_rejected_log_probs,
   677→                    policy_chosen_logits,
   678→                    policy_rejected_logits,
   679→                ) = self.concatenated_forward(self._model, batch)
   680→
   681→                policy_chosen_logits_mean = policy_chosen_logits.detach().mean()
   682→                policy_rejected_logits_mean = policy_rejected_logits.detach().mean()
   683→
   684→                # deleting logits here helps reduce (peak) memory usage - we only need them for metric logging
   685→                del policy_chosen_logits, policy_rejected_logits
   686→
   687→                with torch.no_grad(), disable_adapter(self._model):
   688→                    (
   689→                        reference_chosen_log_probs,
   690→                        reference_rejected_log_probs,
   691→                        _,
   692→                        _,
   693→                    ) = self.concatenated_forward(self._model, batch)
   694→                loss, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards = self._loss_fn(
   695→                    policy_chosen_log_probs,
   696→                    policy_rejected_log_probs,
   697→                    reference_chosen_log_probs,
   698→                    reference_rejected_log_probs,
   699→                )
   700→
   701→                loss = loss.mean()
   702→                reward_accuracies = (chosen_rewards > rejected_rewards).float()
   703→
   704→                loss = loss / self._gradient_accumulation_steps
   705→                running_loss += loss
   706→                loss.backward()
   707→
   708→                # Step with optimizer
   709→                if (idx + 1) % self._gradient_accumulation_steps == 0:
   710→                    self._optimizer.step()
   711→                    self._optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
   712→                    self._lr_scheduler.step()
   713→
   714→                    # Update the number of steps when the weights are updated
   715→                    self.global_step += 1
   716→
   717→                    loss_to_log = running_loss.item()
   718→                    pbar.update(1)
   719→                    pbar.set_description(
   720→                        f"{curr_epoch + 1}|{self.global_step}|Loss: {loss_to_log}"
   721→                    )
   722→
   723→                    # Log per-step metrics
   724→                    if (
   725→                        self.global_step % self._log_every_n_steps == 0
   726→                        and self._is_rank_zero
   727→                    ):
   728→                        time_per_step = time.perf_counter() - t0
   729→                        log_dict = {
   730→                            "loss": loss_to_log,
   731→                            "lr": self._optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"],
   732→                            "tokens_per_second_per_gpu": num_tokens / time_per_step,
   733→                            "rewards/chosen": chosen_rewards.mean().cpu(),
   734→                            "rewards/rejected": rejected_rewards.mean().cpu(),
   735→                            "rewards/accuracies": reward_accuracies.mean().cpu(),
   736→                            "rewards/margins": (chosen_rewards - rejected_rewards)
   737→                            .mean()
   738→                            .cpu(),
   739→                            "log_probs/rejected": policy_rejected_log_probs.detach()
   740→                            .mean()
   741→                            .cpu(),
   742→                            "log_probs/chosen": policy_chosen_log_probs.detach()
   743→                            .mean()
   744→                            .cpu(),
   745→                            "logits/rejected": policy_rejected_logits_mean.cpu(),
   746→                            "logits/chosen": policy_chosen_logits_mean.cpu(),
   747→                        }
   748→                        if self._log_peak_memory_stats:
   749→                            log_dict.update(
   750→                                training.get_memory_stats(device=self._device)
   751→                            )
   752→                        self._metric_logger.log_dict(
   753→                            log_dict,
   754→                            step=self.global_step,
   755→                        )
   756→
   757→                    # Reset running stats for the next step
   758→                    running_loss = 0
   759→                    num_tokens = 0

text: I investigated and fixed the distributed DoRA initialization bug, and added a unit-style test to reproduce and verify the behavior. What was wrong - In recipes/lora_finetune_distributed.py, DoRA magnitude initialization was happening before the magnitudes were materialized off the meta device. - This left a magnitude parameter on the meta device, causing training.validate_no_params_on_meta_device to fail under FSDP. - We must not reassign Parameter objects after FSDP wrapping; instead, we must materialize via state_dict with assign=True to preserve parameter identity. Minimal fix implemented - In recipes/lora_finetune_distributed.py, I changed the ordering so that DoRA magnitudes are materialized off meta via training.load_dora_magnitudes(model) before any initialize_dora_magnitude calls. - Then, for each DoRA module, initialize_dora_magnitude() is called. - This preserves parameter identity for FSDP and ensures all parameters are off the meta device before validation. Patched code snippet (ordering change) - Replaced the previous DoRA block: - was: iterate modules -> initialize_dora_magnitude, then if is_dora: load_dora_magnitudes(model) - now: detect DoRA -> load_dora_magnitudes(model) first, then call initialize_dora_magnitude() on each module Added reproduction test - File: tests/recipes/test_lora_finetune_distributed.py - New test: test_dora_magnitude_materialized_before_initialize - Creates a tiny DoRA-enabled model on the meta device using the same config paths as the recipe. - Initializes LoRA A/B weights off meta. - Materializes base weights via training.load_from_full_model_state_dict. - Crucially: calls load_dora_magnitudes(model) before initialize_dora_magnitude on DoRA modules. - Finally, runs training.validate_no_params_on_meta_device(model) to ensure no parameters remain on meta. - This is CPU-only and does not require multiple GPUs. Why this works - load_dora_magnitudes(model) uses model.load_state_dict(..., assign=True), preserving parameter identity and correctly materializing parameters off meta in an FSDP-safe way. - After materialization, initialize_dora_magnitude() can safely copy into the magnitude parameter. - The validation step confirms there are no meta tensors left. Files changed - recipes/lora_finetune_distributed.py - Adjusted DoRA handling order: - Call load_dora_magnitudes(model) first - Then call initialize_dora_magnitude() - Keep validate_missing_and_unexpected_for_lora(...) and training.validate_no_params_on_meta_device(model) as-is at the end. - tests/recipes/test_lora_finetune_distributed.py - Added test_dora_magnitude_materialized_before_initialize as described above. How to run the new test - The test is CPU-only and unit-style: - python -m pytest tests/recipes/test_lora_finetune_distributed.py::TestLoRAFinetuneDistributedRecipe::test_dora_magnitude_materialized_before_initialize -q - Optionally, run the whole file: - python -m pytest tests/recipes/test_lora_finetune_distributed.py -q - Integration tests requiring 2 GPUs are decorated to skip if not available. Notes - I did not reassign any Parameters post-FSDP wrapping. - I kept changes minimal and scoped to the distributed LoRA finetune recipe, per the task requirements. - I did not commit changes.
